Re: Appeal of Medical-Necessity Denial  
Requested service: ACL reconstruction  
CPT: 29888  
Reference number: POC-A0C827A88A-54850  
Date of denial notice: August 18, 2026

To the Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for arthroscopically aided anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, CPT 29888. The denial states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan’s criteria for medical necessity. Based on the clinical records submitted with the prior authorization request, the procedure is medically necessary to treat a complete ACL tear causing persistent symptoms and recurrent functional instability.

The records establish the following:

- I have had nine months of progressive knee pain that has not resolved with rest.
- MRI performed on June 22, 2026, shows a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with an associated bone-bruise pattern.
- The menisci are intact and there is no significant arthritis, supporting the ACL tear as the principal structural cause of the symptoms.
- I have recurrent instability with pivoting and have experienced two episodes of giving way on stairs.
- Physical examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- Conservative treatment has been substantial and unsuccessful. I completed 20 supervised physical-therapy visits over eight weeks, from May 21, 2026, through July 16, 2026, focused on range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing.
- I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 7, 2026, produced only four weeks of partial relief.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance-use condition. I am a nonsmoker, with a BMI of 29.

These findings demonstrate a documented complete ACL disruption, persistent pain, recurrent instability, objective examination abnormalities, and failure of appropriate nonoperative treatment. Continuing conservative treatment has not corrected the torn ligament or prevented further episodes of instability. ACL reconstruction is therefore directed at the documented structural injury and functional instability rather than being treatment for routine degenerative arthritis.

The public Meridian/Ambetter materials I was able to locate do not provide a specific publicly available medical-necessity policy containing the criteria applied to CPT 29888. Accordingly, this appeal does not quote a plan policy. Please identify the exact guideline or clinical-review criteria used for this denial, including the guideline or vendor name, version, effective date, and each criterion that the reviewer determined was not satisfied. Please also provide the clinical rationale and records relied upon in making the determination.

Please reconsider and approve prior authorization for CPT 29888. If the denial is upheld, please provide a detailed written explanation addressing each of the clinical facts above and explaining why a complete MRI-confirmed ACL tear with recurrent giving-way episodes and failed conservative treatment does not satisfy the criteria applied to this request.

Please acknowledge receipt of this appeal and send the appeal determination to me and to my treating orthopedic surgeon, Duval, MD.

Sincerely,

Riley Hayes  
[Signature]  
[Date signed]

Enclosures:

- MRI report dated June 22, 2026
- Physical-therapy discharge note documenting 20 visits from May 21, 2026, through July 16, 2026
- Medication and injection treatment history
- Orthopedic examination and clinical records
- Copy of the denial notice
- Any additional records submitted by Duval, MD
